name: Alaska Driver License — New & Renewal
agency: Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles
description: Apply for a new Alaska driver license or renew an existing one. The Division of Motor Vehicles issues standard and REAL ID-compliant credentials at all office locations; many renewals, replacements, and address changes can be done online without an office visit.
eligibility: Alaska resident applying for a first license, transferring an out-of-state license, or renewing an expiring license

Pass vision, knowledge, and road tests for a first-time license
Surrender any valid out-of-state driver license

Social Security number
Proof of Alaska residential address
Payment for the license fee

applyLinks.label: DMV online services (renewals, replacements, appointments)

name: Alaska Vehicle Registration & Title
agency: Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles

Buyer of a new or used vehicle (dealer must apply for title transfer within 30 days of purchase)

deadlines.note: Rolling — renew before the expiration date on your registration; biennial registration options vary by vehicle type

Application for Title & Registration (Form 812) for new registrations and title transfers
VIN inspection where required

Lien information if the vehicle is financed
Proof of insurance
Payment for registration and title fees

applyLinks.label: DMV online services (renew registration, update address)

name: DenaliCare — Alaska Medicaid
agency: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance

U.S. citizen, national, or qualified non-citizen

agency: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance
description: SNAP helps eligible low-income households buy food, with benefits loaded monthly onto the Alaska Quest EBT card. Households relying substantially on subsistence hunting and fishing can also use benefits for gear like nets, hooks, rods, and harpoons.

Provide income, resource, and household verification

agency: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Employment and Training Services
description: File for Alaska unemployment insurance benefits if you lost work through no fault of your own. First-time claims must be filed by phone with a claim center; renewals, weekly certifications, and payment status are available online through myAlaska.
eligibility: Earned wages in work covered by Alaska UI law during the base period
Unemployed through no fault of your own (layoff, reduction in hours, or qualifying separation)
Able, available, and actively seeking full-time work
Registered for work with the Alaska Employment Service or your union

File a new or reopened claim (first-time filers must call a claim center)
Register for work and complete required work-search activities
whatToBring: Full legal name and Social Security number
Work authorization if not a U.S. citizen or resident
Employer names, addresses, and dates of employment for the last 18 months
Reason for separation from each employer

applyLinks.label: File unemployment benefits online (myAlaska)

name: Alaska Voter Registration
agency: Alaska Division of Elections
description: Register to vote or update your registration in Alaska. Residents are automatically registered to vote when they apply for the Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD) and have 30 days to opt out. Online registration requires a current Alaska driver license or state ID.
eligibility: U.S. citizen and Alaska resident
At least 18 years old (or within 90 days of 18th birthday to register)
Resident of the state and election district for at least 30 days before voting
Not disqualified by a felony conviction involving moral turpitude unless voting rights restored

deadlines.label: Registration cutoff
deadlines.note: Register or update registration at least 30 days before an election; PFD applicants are auto-registered unless they opt out within 30 days

prerequisites: Current Alaska driver license or state ID to register online
Proof of Alaska residency when initially registering from outside the state
Cancel any voter registration in another state
whatToBring: Alaska driver license or state ID
For paper registration: copy of driver license, state ID, passport, or birth certificate
Proof of Alaska residency if registering from outside the state (e.g., hunting/fishing license, LES, employment proof)

applyLinks.label: Register or update voter registration

cost: Free

name: Alaska Business Registration — LLC & Corporation Formation
agency: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Corporations Section
description: Form an LLC, corporation, or other business entity in Alaska through the Corporations Section. File articles of organization or incorporation online or by mail, and keep the entity in good standing with biennial reports.
eligibility: Any person forming a domestic entity or registering a foreign entity to do business in Alaska
Entity name must be distinguishable from existing Alaska entities
Every corporation and LLC must maintain a registered agent with a street address in Alaska

deadlines.label: Filing
deadlines.note: Rolling — file before transacting business; biennial reports due every two years

prerequisites: Distinguishable business name (search the corporations database first)
Registered agent with an Alaska street address
Articles of organization (LLC) or incorporation (corporation)
whatToBring: Proposed entity name and NAICS business activity codes
Registered agent name and Alaska street address
Names and addresses of organizers, members, or directors
Payment for the filing fee

applyLinks.label: Create or file for a new entity (Corporations Section)

cost: $250 to form an LLC; biennial report $100

name: Alaska State Taxes — No Individual Income Tax
agency: Alaska Department of Revenue, Tax Division
description: Alaska has no individual income tax and no statewide sales tax — individuals file only federal returns. The Tax Division administers business taxes (including a graduated corporate income tax for C corporations with Alaska-source income), and cities and boroughs may levy local sales taxes.
eligibility: Individuals: no state income tax return required regardless of income
Businesses: corporate income tax applies to C corporations with Alaska-source income
Remote sellers meeting economic nexus thresholds must collect applicable local sales taxes

deadlines.label: Individual filing
deadlines.note: No state individual return to file — file your federal return by the IRS deadline; check city/borough local tax deadlines if you run a business

prerequisites: No registration needed for individuals — there is nothing to file with the state
Businesses register for applicable tax types through Revenue Online
whatToBring: For federal filing: W-2s, 1099s, and federal records
Proof of Alaska residency for programs like the PFD if needed
Business filers: federal return copies, estimated payment records, local sales tax registrations

applyLinks.label: Alaska Tax Division (business tax filing via Revenue Online)

cost: No individual income tax to file; business tax fees vary by tax type

name: Alaska Professional Licensing — MY LICENSE Portal
agency: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing
description: Alaska's central licensing portal for more than 40 professions — nursing, real estate, construction contractors, barbers, engineers, medical, and more. Use the MY LICENSE self-service portal (with a myAlaska account) to apply, renew, update contact information, and print license certificates.
eligibility: Applicants meeting the education, examination, and experience requirements of the specific board or program
Licensees renewing before expiration (no grace period — lapsed licenses cannot be used to practice)
Out-of-state applicants may qualify for licensure by endorsement or credential depending on the profession

deadlines.label: Renewal
deadlines.note: Rolling — renew by the expiration date on your license; renewal schedules vary by profession (e.g., nursing renews in even-numbered years)

prerequisites: myAlaska account linked to your license via the MY LICENSE portal
Meet board-specific education and examination requirements
Professional fitness (background) disclosure where required
whatToBring: myAlaska login credentials
License number and web authorization code to link an existing license
Education transcripts, exam scores, and work verification per board requirements
Payment for application and license fees

applyLinks.label: Professional licensing portal and MY LICENSE

cost: Varies by profession and board (application, license, and renewal fees)

name: Alaska Birth Certificate — Vital Records
agency: Alaska Department of Health, Bureau of Vital Statistics
description: Order a certified copy of an Alaska birth certificate from the Bureau of Vital Statistics. Request by mail or fax, in person in Anchorage, Fairbanks, or Juneau, or online through VitalChek for expedited service.
eligibility: The person named on the record, a parent, legal representative with documentation, or an entitled party
Only the person named, parents, or legal representatives may order; others must show legal entitlement
State office holds records back to the 1890s (many events before 1930 were never registered)

deadlines.label: Orders
deadlines.note: Rolling — regular mail orders processed in about 2–3 weeks; expedited (fax) orders in about 3 business days; heirloom certificates in 4–6 weeks

prerequisites: Completed birth certificate request form with original signature
Copy of the applicant's photo ID (or notarized signature)
Proof of relationship or legal documentation if ordering for someone other than yourself or your child
whatToBring: Signed request form
Copy of government-issued photo ID (enlarge and lighten for readability)
Proof of relationship if applicable
Payment (check or money order for mail; cash accepted for walk-in only)

applyLinks.label: Order expedited birth certificate through VitalChek
Alaska birth certificate request form (PDF)

cost: $30 first certified copy; $25 each additional copy of the same record; heirloom certificates $55

name: Alaska Temporary Assistance Program (ATAP) — TANF
agency: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance
description: ATAP is Alaska's TANF program, providing monthly cash assistance to eligible low-income families with children to meet basic needs. Benefits are paid on the Alaska Quest EBT card, and adults are connected to work and training activities.
eligibility: Families with dependent children and household income within ATAP limits
Alaska resident; U.S. citizen, national, or qualified non-citizen
Adults must cooperate with work requirements, child support enforcement, and the Personal Responsibility Plan
Federal 60-month lifetime limit on cash benefits applies (with exemptions)

deadlines.label: Applications

prerequisites: Complete an application and eligibility interview with a Division of Public Assistance caseworker
Provide identity, income, residency, and household verification

Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment statements)
Proof of Alaska residency (lease, utility bills)
Birth certificates for dependent children

applyLinks.label: Apply for ATAP via Alaska Connect

name: Alaska State Parks — Annual Parking Pass & Camping
agency: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Parks and Outdoor Recreation
description: Alaska State Parks charges no general entry fee; instead, day-use parking areas and boat launches use fee decals, and campgrounds charge nightly fees. An annual day-use parking pass covers a calendar year of parking at most parks; disabled veterans get a free multi-year camping pass.
eligibility: Open to everyone — passes sold at Public Information Centers, ranger stations, and online
Disabled veterans with a service-connected disability qualify for a free 5-year camping pass
No senior discount is offered for park passes

deadlines.note: Annual passes are valid for the calendar year; buy anytime. Some reservable cabins and campsites book on a rolling 3-month window

Campsite and cabin reservations through the Alaska State Parks reservation system (new system launched Oct 1, 2026)
whatToBring: Annual parking decal affixed to the lower driver-side windshield
Boat launch decal affixed to the trailer tongue for boat launches
Disabled veterans: proof of service-connected disability for the free camping pass

applyLinks.label: Buy annual parking and boat launch passes

agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)
